chapter: Trumpet styles and early New Orleans scene
title: Sitting in with Louis Armstrong and Louis's style
summary: Punch tells how he sat in on his return from the Army and says Louis took famous ideas from street players.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Well, Chris was a nice man with a plunger, you know. He was a plunger man. Yeah, I know. Well, I'm going to tell you how this happened. When I first came here from the Army, somebody carried me down to 25, where Louis was playing. And I got up there and played two numbers over there and some other song I played. And oh, that's the, let me see what, no, Kid Olive wasn't there. There's Kid Orange, Johnny Dots, Baby Dots, Lorenzo Stahl on guitar, and Bob Lyons on bass. That's how it was. And I played them two tunes and got to kidding Louis about it. Louis got mad boy. I told him, you take him, I'll just go ahead on, let's take him on in the band. So they said, oh no man, we're just kidding. So from then on, I just said, Louis was a great little trumpet player, he was younger than me though. But he was crazy about me playing. I was working at that storage, you know, when I got a job. And he had to go to the boat out on the river there. And he'd get right across the street up there and watch up there and be playing for hours before he'd go to white. Way back when he'd get ready to go. He's crazy about my playing.
Well was Louis copying anybody at that time? Did he have his own style already?

I think he did. Tell me one thing he did, he always had his own style playing, but what he did do, the stuff that he got famous with, he took it right from here. All the stuff that he, you know, heebie jeebies and all that kind of stuff. Well he got that from, I sure the boys was playing that up in the streets here, but they didn't know what he was doing, you know. And Louis just went up there and made something out of it, see.
